validated_results.title: Alcohol consumption and the risk of renal cancers in the European prospective investigation into cancer and nutrition (EPIC).
validated_results.reason: Prospective EPIC cohort reporting hazard ratios for total alcohol consumption and incident renal cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: first higher category of total alcohol consumption at recruitment versus light drinkers
extraction.timing: baseline alcohol consumption assessed at recruitment, 1992-2010 follow-up
extraction.population: men and women in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition cohort

sample_size.excerpt: From 1992 through to 2010, 477,325 men and women in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition cohort were followed for incident renal cancers (n = 931).

cases.excerpt: From 1992 through to 2010, 477,325 men and women in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition cohort were followed for incident renal cancers (n = 931).

effect_size.excerpt: In multivariate analysis, total alcohol consumption at baseline was inversely associated with renal cancer; the HR and 95% CI for the increasing categories of total alcohol consumption at recruitment versus the light drinkers category were 0.78 (0.62-0.99), 0.82 (0.64-1.04), 0.70 (0.55-0.90), 0.91 (0.63-1.30), respectively, (ptrend = 0.001). A similar relationship was observed for average lifetime alcohol consumption and for all renal cancer subsites combined or for renal parenchyma subsite.

confidence_interval.excerpt: In multivariate analysis, total alcohol consumption at baseline was inversely associated with renal cancer; the HR and 95% CI for the increasing categories of total alcohol consumption at recruitment versus the light drinkers category were 0.78 (0.62-0.99), 0.82 (0.64-1.04), 0.70 (0.55-0.90), 0.91 (0.63-1.30), respectively, (ptrend = 0.001).

comparison.excerpt: increasing categories of total alcohol consumption at recruitment versus the light drinkers category

design.excerpt: Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated from Cox proportional hazard models.

continent.excerpt: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition cohort

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Baseline and lifetime alcohol consumption was assessed by country-specific, validated dietary questionnaires.
